diagrams.title: Buy the Exit Before You Buy the Lot
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages from auction discovery to collected resale
diagrams.assumptions_note: GSA Auctions, GovPlanet, GovDeals, and Public Surplus are discovery channels, not interchangeable sellers or uniform contract regimes. Verify the actual seller, governing sale terms, and asset restrictions for every lot. Revenue means the operator's gross resale proceeds, not auction-platform transaction volume.
diagrams.caption: A low hammer price creates no profit until removal, condition, documentation, and buyer payment are resolved.

stages.label: Source qualified lots
stages.detail: Configure auction alerts by equipment class, pickup radius, closing date, and seller. Match each candidate to recent resale evidence and named prospective business buyers before requesting inspection.

stages.label: Inspect and price
stages.detail: Record serial numbers, condition, title documents, loading constraints, and removal deadlines. Set the hammer ceiling from expected collected resale less fees, freight, repairs, labor, carrying costs, overhead allocation, and required profit.

stages.label: Bid and settle
stages.detail: Use a versioned bid-limit worksheet; reserve cash for the full invoice and removal plan before bidding. Validate payment instructions through the auction account and seller contact details before sending a bank payment.

stages.label: Remove and prepare
stages.detail: Book the carrier within the contractual pickup window. Photograph condition at release and receipt, attach costs to the inventory record, and stop repairs when the remaining resale contribution falls below the approved floor.

stages.label: Remarket and collect
stages.detail: Publish tested specifications and disclosed defects, execute the applicable title or bill-of-sale transfer, verify payment receipt rather than screenshots, and reconcile proceeds, direct costs, and inventory age.

diagrams.title: Track One Cohort from Alert to Cash
diagrams.subtitle: A nested 200-lot cohort with six completed resale collections
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative 120-day observation window, not a forecast of market conversion rates or a promise of first-month sales. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; count each lot once. The canonical time to first deal remains 1–6 months.
diagrams.caption: The two awarded but uncollected lots remain inventory or unsettled dispositions; they do not become collected resale proceeds merely because an auction was won.

stages.label: Unique alerted lots
stages.detail: Deduplicate reposted listings and capture seller, asset class, location, closing date, and pickup window. This is the complete cohort denominator.

stages.label: Desk-qualified lots
stages.detail: Retain only lots within the operating radius, capital limit, permitted asset categories, and documented buyer demand. Exclude inaccessible removal sites and unresolved ownership restrictions.

stages.label: Inspection-cleared lots
stages.detail: Complete condition verification, document review, transport quotations, and repair estimates. These 24 lots receive evidence-backed bid ceilings; inspection expense also includes unsuccessful bids.

stages.label: Awarded and paid lots
stages.detail: Win eight lots without exceeding their ceilings and settle their purchase invoices. Reject price chasing; the other sixteen cleared lots consume inspection effort but no acquisition principal.

stages.label: Resold and collected lots
stages.detail: Collect resale proceeds on six of the eight acquired lots within the observation window. Overall alert-to-collection conversion is 3%; track the remaining two lots through inventory aging.

diagrams.title: $575,000 Resale Proceeds Become $80,500 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile the canonical Base-Case 14.0% net margin
diagrams.assumptions_note: USD per year. Opening and closing bars are totals; the four intermediate bars are negative cost movements. The scorecard fixes revenue and owner net, while the cost-category split is an illustrative operating budget. Direct handling and repair labor belong in their respective direct-cost categories; remaining operating labor belongs in overhead.
diagrams.caption: $575,000 - $345,000 - $46,000 - $46,000 - $57,500 = $80,500; $80,500 / $575,000 = 14.0%. Sales tax collected for remittance is excluded from resale revenue.

stages.label: Gross resale proceeds
stages.detail: Canonical Base-Case annual operator revenue from owned surplus inventory resales. This is neither client asset value nor a marketplace's aggregate transaction volume.

stages.label: Inventory acquisition
stages.detail: Allocate purchase prices, buyer premiums, and nonrecoverable acquisition taxes to units sold. Recoverable taxes are excluded; unsold inventory remains a separate working-capital exposure.

stages.label: Transport and handling
stages.detail: Include loading, rigging, carrier charges, fuel surcharges, direct handling labor, and delivery costs associated with completed resales. Missed pickup windows can exhaust this entire allowance.

stages.label: Inspection and refurbishment
stages.detail: Budget inspection effort, parts, testing, cleaning, and repair-contractor labor. Include inspections that produce no winning bid and avoid counting the same labor again in overhead.

stages.label: Operating overhead
stages.detail: Allocate remaining operating labor, storage, insurance, software, selling and payment fees, administration, and operating-loss allowances. The monthly equivalent is $4,791.67, within the canonical $3,000–$15,000 monthly opex range.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.detail: Canonical Base-Case residual after the four expense categories for a two-full-time, three-contractor pod. Owner distributions do not create an additional expense below this closing total.

diagrams.title: Compare Sub-Niches on the Same Cost Boundary
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative contribution before operating overhead, not net margin
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each bar assumes $10,000 of realized resale revenue. Direct costs include acquisition, transport, handling, inspection, and refurbishment; operating overhead, including selling and payment fees, is excluded. These percentages are planning hypotheses, not measured auction yields. An equal-revenue mix averages 24% direct contribution, matching the Base-Case before its 10% overhead allocation.
diagrams.caption: A larger spread can conceal slower turnover, expensive removal, or unsold inventory. Validate each hypothesis with completed transactions before increasing bid limits.

stages.label: Office furniture bundles
stages.detail: $10,000 resale less $8,400 direct cost leaves $1,600 before overhead. Require confirmed loading access and buyer measurements; bulky low-value pieces can turn storage into the dominant cost.

stages.label: Commercial kitchen equipment
stages.detail: $10,000 resale less $8,000 direct cost leaves $2,000 before overhead. Verify power, gas, refrigeration condition, and installation requirements; unverified functionality can overwhelm repair limits.

stages.label: Fleet vehicles and trailers
stages.detail: $10,000 resale less $7,600 direct cost leaves $2,400 before overhead. Match VINs to sale documents and confirm the state title pathway before allowing transport or repair spending.

stages.label: Grounds-maintenance equipment
stages.detail: $10,000 resale less $7,200 direct cost leaves $2,800 before overhead. Inspect hydraulic systems, hour meters, attachments, and seasonal demand; missing proprietary components can erase the spread.

stages.label: Industrial shop equipment
stages.detail: $10,000 resale less $6,800 direct cost leaves $3,200 before overhead. Confirm rigging access, three-phase power requirements, guarding condition, and a credible buyer before bidding.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before an Irrevocable Bid
diagrams.subtitle: Proceed only when every branch has documented supporting evidence
diagrams.assumptions_note: Read the four nodes sequentially: a documented pass moves to the next node; an unresolved issue stops the bid. Federal sale rules do not automatically govern municipal sales. California citations illustrate state-specific requirements and must be replaced or supplemented for the actual operating jurisdiction.
diagrams.caption: Auction access, title evidence, restricted-property rules, and removal economics are separate checks; clearing one does not resolve the others.

stages.label: Seller authority and eligibility
stages.detail: For federal lots, review 40 U.S.C. 545, 41 CFR Part 102-38, and the specific sale terms. For municipal lots, verify the seller's authority and local conditions. Record bidder eligibility, deposit requirements, payment deadlines, and authorized purchasing identity.

stages.label: Ownership and title pathway
stages.detail: Match VIN or serial number to the sale record. For federal vehicles, establish whether SF-97 or another title document will be delivered and whether the state accepts that pathway. Review applicable dealer licensing and transfer duties, including California Vehicle Code sections 11700 and 5900 when operating there.

stages.label: Restricted property and DEMIL
stages.detail: Review the listing's demilitarization instructions, end-use terms, and controlled-property conditions. Exclude lots whose obligations exceed documented capability or authorization. Evaluate export restrictions separately under 15 CFR 736.2 and 22 CFR 121.1 where applicable; an SF-97 does not waive those restrictions.

stages.label: Permits, removal, and cash capacity
stages.value: Pass: funded plan; stop: uncovered obligation
stages.detail: Confirm applicable seller permits, resale-certificate treatment, and tax collection obligations; California Revenue and Taxation Code section 6071 is one state example. Require carrier availability, site access, insurance, repair limits, and sufficient cash through the contractual removal deadline.

diagrams.title: Five Core Seats, Two Explicit Scale Additions
diagrams.subtitle: Base: 2 FT + 3 C; scaled operation: 3 FT + 4 C
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time and C means contractor. The first five seats form the Conservative and Base-Case pod; the final two seats are additions for the Scaled Small-Team scenario. Contractor headcount does not imply full-time hours, and seat descriptions do not set compensation.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $150,000 revenue × 8% = $12,000 owner net with five people. Base: $575,000 × 14% = $80,500 with five. Scaled: $1,000,000 × 20% = $200,000 with seven. All revenue is gross operator resale proceeds.

stages.label: FT 1: commercial owner
stages.value: Core seat; bid and cash authority
stages.detail: Own buyer demand, final bid ceilings, funding allocation, seller exceptions, and inventory markdown decisions. Review cash committed by pickup deadline before authorizing another purchase.

stages.label: FT 2: inventory and remarketing lead
stages.detail: Maintain asset records, photograph condition, coordinate preparation, publish listings, qualify buyers, and verify fulfillment. Reconcile serial numbers across receipt, repair, and sale documents.

stages.label: C 1: transport and rigging specialist
stages.detail: Quote loading and freight before bidding, reserve pickup capacity, document custody, and deliver within site restrictions. Escalate missing forklifts, access constraints, and loading damage immediately.

stages.label: C 2: inspection and repair technician
stages.value: Core seat; condition and repair control
stages.detail: Perform asset-class inspections, produce defect estimates, execute bounded repairs, and record test results. Seek a revised commercial decision before exceeding the authorized repair ceiling.

stages.label: C 3: title and bookkeeping specialist
stages.detail: Track title submissions, resale documentation, tax records, purchase invoices, and bank receipts. Separate tax liabilities, inventory cash, direct costs, and overhead in the asset-level ledger.

stages.label: FT 3: operations lead
stages.detail: Add dedicated scheduling, yard control, carrier coordination, and cycle-time ownership when concurrent lots exceed the core team's capacity. The commercial owner retains final bid authority.

stages.label: C 4: field inspection specialist
stages.detail: Expand inspection coverage without substituting listing photographs for condition evidence. Use standard test sheets and return inspection findings before the bid worksheet is finalized.

diagrams.title: Protect Removal Cash Before Expanding Inventory
diagrams.subtitle: Four allocation buckets across $25,000, $100,000, and $200,000
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values show the $100,000 reference budget in USD. Each stage also provides its allocation at the canonical $25,000 minimum and $200,000 maximum. The allocation percentages are illustrative and sum to 100% at every capital level. Startup deployment is not annual revenue or annual expense.
diagrams.caption: Minimum: $15,000 + $3,750 + $2,500 + $3,750 = $25,000. Reference: $60,000 + $15,000 + $10,000 + $15,000 = $100,000. Maximum: $120,000 + $30,000 + $20,000 + $30,000 = $200,000.

stages.label: Acquisition working capital
stages.detail: Allocate $15,000 at minimum capital and $120,000 at maximum capital. Cover hammer prices, premiums, and acquisition cash obligations while limiting concentration in any single lot or buyer segment.

stages.label: Removal and repair float
stages.detail: Allocate $3,750 at minimum capital and $30,000 at maximum capital. Ring-fence loading, freight, inspection, testing, and bounded repair payments that fall due before resale collections.

stages.label: Facilities and operating setup
stages.detail: Allocate $2,500 at minimum capital and $20,000 at maximum capital. Fund appropriately scaled storage deposits, insurance setup, safety equipment, inventory controls, and required business registrations.

stages.label: Liquidity and holding reserve
stages.detail: Allocate $3,750 at minimum capital and $30,000 at maximum capital. Preserve cash for delayed collections, additional storage, and operating disruptions; calculate runway from actual monthly burn rather than assuming six months are funded.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Backed Buying Operation
diagrams.subtitle: Launch controls and buyer coverage before forcing a first purchase
diagrams.assumptions_note: Milestones describe controllable setup work, not required sales outcomes. Canonical time to first deal is 1–6 months. If no lot passes the documented bid criteria, complete the sprint with a qualified watchlist and retained cash.
diagrams.caption: Auction alerts, bid-limit worksheets, and inventory tracking support the operator; none replaces inspection, title verification, removal capacity, or buyer demand.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.detail: Choose two initial asset classes and a pickup radius. Review seller terms and applicable permits, create a restricted-property exclusion list, and obtain storage, insurance, and carrier quotations. Deliver a written buying mandate and capital budget.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Build buyer evidence and unit economics
stages.detail: Interview ten prospective business buyers and document specifications, delivery constraints, and payment practices. Configure GSA Auctions, GovPlanet, GovDeals, and Public Surplus alerts. Price five candidate lots using resale evidence and complete landed-cost bid worksheets.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.detail: Arrange inspections for up to three qualified lots when access is available. Resolve title documents, obtain written freight estimates, assign pod responsibilities, and test inventory records. Bid only when the four pre-flight checks pass.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Execute conditionally and review the cohort
stages.detail: If awarded a qualifying lot, settle and remove it on the seller's timetable, record actual condition, and begin buyer outreach. Otherwise continue qualification. Review cash commitments, inspection losses, inventory aging, and expected versus actual landed costs.
